body: Gradient-based data attribution has become an important tool for high-quality data selection in the instruction fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), as it estimates the contribution of training examples through their influence on model optimization. However, we find that existing global gradient attribution methods suffer from surface-form bias: minor changes to semantically irrelevant details, such as wording or formatting, can produce highly inconsistent attribution scores even when the underlying content remains unchanged. To address this issue, we propose Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution (CIGA), a robust framework for instruction data selection. CIGA first identifies layers whose gradients are both influential for attribution and stable under semantics-preserving surface-form perturbations, thereby reducing formatting noise in gradient features. It then dynamically fuses these attribution signals with semantic representations of the input, combining optimization-level influence with content-level information. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show that CIGA produces more stable rankings under surface-form perturbations while preserving downstream capabilities and improving average performance. CIGA also reduces attribution cost, offering a robust and efficient approach to data selection for LLM instruction tuning.
summaryZh: 通过内容不变梯度归因进行稳健的LLM数据选择。基于梯度的数据归因已成为大型语言模型（LLM）指令微调中高质量数据选择的重要工具，因为它通过训练实例对模型优化的影响来估计训练实例的贡献。然而，我们发现现有的全局梯度归因方法存在表面形式偏差：即使底层内容保持不变，语义上不相关的细节（例如措辞或格式）的微小变化也可能产生高度不一致的归因分数。
